paragraphs.text: Heb., Ye that pursue or follow hard after it, as Paul did. {Php 3:13-14} The speech is directed to those Jews that embraced the gospel; persuading them to persist in the faith, "in nothing terrified by their adversaries," since Almighty God would keep and help them, as he had done faithful Abraham and Sarah, their ancestors; to whom also he would of stones raise up sons {a} in the conversion of the Gentiles, and could do it as easily as he had hewed the Hebrews, that great nation, out of aged Abraham, and superannuated Sarah; who are here compared to a dry rock, and a deep pit.
paragraphs.anchor: Hearken unto me, ye that follow after righteousness.

paragraphs.text: Est honesta periphrasis actus coniugalis. The word here used is of the same root with Nekebah, the female kind of all creatures.
paragraphs.anchor: And to the hole of the pit whence ye were digged.

paragraphs.text: {a} Banim Meabanim.

"Look" and again "look." "Hearken" and again "hearken." These poor Jews, before the coming of Christ in the flesh, were vino somnoque sepulti, drunk with the cup of God’s fury, {Isa 51:17} and so fast asleep, that they needed to be thus roused and raised up to the hope of better times, which now were at hand.
paragraphs.anchor: Look unto Abraham your father.

paragraphs.text: By the force of her faith also, {Heb 11:11} her son Isaac was emeritae fidel filius. Now these domestic examples are alleged to assure them that God could do the like again in respect of spiritual children, Abraham’s right seed. {Gal 4:22-31}
paragraphs.anchor: And unto Sarah that bare you.

paragraphs.text: Be not ye therefore troubled at your aloneness.
paragraphs.anchor: For I called him alone.

paragraphs.text: God’s benediction is his benefaction; the Pope’s is not so; fumos vendit, fumo pereat.
paragraphs.anchor: And blessed him, and increased him.

paragraphs.text: (As once he did Abraham) by multiplying her children, giving her good store of converts. These were the apostles and the primitive Christians, those earthly angels, who made the world, which before was as a waste wilderness, to become a most pleasant and plentiful paradise. Chrysostom somewhere calleth them angels, and saith that they were puriores coelo afflictione facti, more clear than the azured sky.
paragraphs.anchor: For the Lord shall comfort Zion.

paragraphs.text: i.e., The gospel of grace, that "perfect law of liberty," "the law of the spirit of life." {Rom 8:2}
paragraphs.anchor: For a law shall proceed from me

paragraphs.text: I will firmly and irrevocably establish the government of my word and Spirit in the Church for a secure guide to bring it to eternal life. Some {a} render it thus, "My judgment," i.e., my gospel, shall be for a light of the people, whereby I will give rest. So that here is a double effect of the gospel, viz., saving light, and peace of conscience.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will make my judgment to rest.

i.e., My faithfulness, or my Son, that Sun of righteousness, is already on the way, {a} and will be with you forthwith.

paragraphs.anchor: Fear ye not the reproach of men.

paragraphs.text: They shall be crushed before the moth, {Job 4:19} that is, easily be destroyed, and their own consciences shall grub upon them too throughout all eternity.

paragraphs.text: Bear therefore bravely all contumelies and contempts of men.

paragraphs.text: God had promised what his holy arm should do for his people, {Isa 51:5} now they beg of him to use it, and bestir himself for their relief and rescue; and this they do magno affectu atque animi impetu, heartily wishing the coming of Christ and the declaration of the gospel to their salvation.
paragraphs.anchor: Awake, awake, O arm of the Lord.

paragraphs.text: God seemeth sometimes to be asleep, and we must wake him; to delay, and we must quicken him; to have lost his compassions, which yet never fail, and we must find them for him.
paragraphs.anchor: Awake, as in the ancient days.

paragraphs.text: Or, Hewed Egypt with thy ten plagues successively, though she were a proud and potent state.
paragraphs.anchor: Art not thou it that hath cut Rahab?

paragraphs.text: Or, Crocodile; that is, Pharaoh, {Psa 74:14} whom thou didst put to pain, even the "pains of a travailing woman" (as the word signifieth), when he sank "as a millstone in the mighty waters."
paragraphs.anchor: And wounded the dragon.

paragraphs.text: And canst not thou do as much again for thy poor people? This is an excellent way of arguing with God in prayer - viz., from his ancient acts.
paragraphs.anchor: Art not thou it which hath dried the sea?

paragraphs.text: This is God’s answer, as some; or the good people’s confidence, as others, that God would deliver them now, as he had done their forefathers from Pharaoh.
paragraphs.anchor: Therefore the redeemed of the Lord, &c.

paragraphs.text: As a fair and precious crown. {2Ti 4:8} Some make it a metaphor from those that carry heavy burdens on their heads; St Paul calleth it a "weight of glory."
paragraphs.anchor: And everlasting joy.

paragraphs.anchor: They shall obtain joy.

paragraphs.text: This is certainly an answer to that supplication, {Isa 51:10} and it comprehendeth a reprehension and an expostulation about their pusillanimity, which was more than womanly. Therefore it followeth,
paragraphs.anchor: I, even I, am he that comforteth you.

paragraphs.text: {a} Heb., Thou woman, thou hen hearted creature.
paragraphs.anchor: Who art thou?

paragraphs.text: Heb., Sorry man, ab homine misero, aerumnoso, damnato ad mortem, ab hoste faeneo, An enemy of clouts, as we say. We trouble ourselves oft through ignorance; in the dark everything scares us.
paragraphs.anchor: That thou shouldest be afraid of a man?

paragraphs.text: {a} At, not Atta.

Thou considerest not wisely (1.) How fearfully and wonderfully thou art made; (2.) What a mighty power God put forth in the creation of the whole world; all which he will rather unmake again than thou shalt want seasonable help.
paragraphs.anchor: And forgettest the Lord thy maker.

paragraphs.anchor: And hast feared continually every day.

paragraphs.text: q.d., It is but fury, and not power, and that not illimited neither; for "in the thing wherein they deal proudly, I am above them." {Exo 18:11}
paragraphs.anchor: And where is the fury of the oppressor?

paragraphs.text: i.e., Deliverance is even at the next door by; or, it is a description, saith Diodate, of the believers’ readiness in answering with the motion of their hearts to God’s calling and deliverance.
paragraphs.anchor: The captive exile hasteneth that he may be loosed

paragraphs.text: Or, I the Lord thy God am he that stilleth the sea when the waves of it roar; how much more then can I curb and control the rage of man! "Surely," saith David, "the wrath of man shall praise thee: the remainder of wrath shalt thou restrain"; where the Septuagint have it, It shall keep holiday to thee, εωρταζει σοι.
paragraphs.anchor: For I am the Lord thy God, that divided the sea.

paragraphs.text: O Isaiah, my servant; but especially, O Christ, my Son.
paragraphs.anchor: And I have put my words in thy mouth.

paragraphs.text: God doth as great a wonder, in saying to Zion, "Thou art my people," in the work of renovation, as if he had made a new world. "Whosoever is in Christ is a new creature," or a new creation. {2Co 5:17} Christ is called, "The beginning of the creation of God." {Rev 3:14} Some, by "planting the heavens and laying the foundation of the earth" here, understand the state of the gospel, called by St Peter a "new heaven and a new earth"; and the same, they say, is called by our Saviour "regeneration" in Mat 19:28, "Ye which have followed me in the regeneration," &c.; and by the author to the Hebrews, "The world to come." {Heb 2:5}
paragraphs.anchor: That I may plant the heavens, &c.

paragraphs.text: Suscita te, suscita te. As the Church had stirred up the arm of the Lord to awake, {Isa 51:9} so here he doth the Church, cheering her up, and, as it were, drinking to her in a cup of nepenthe, after her bitter cup of gall and aloes, which she had drunk to drunkenness, and had none to guide her, {Isa 51:18} as a drunken man had need to have.
paragraphs.anchor: Awake, awake.

paragraphs.text: Herein happy yet, that God had a hand in the mingling of thy cup; who, being a wise and gracious physician and father, would be sure not to overdo; for "he knoweth our frame, he remembereth that we are dust." {Psa 103:14}
paragraphs.anchor: That hast drunk at the hand of the Lord.

paragraphs.text: Or, His cup of poison; {Deu 32:24; Deu 32:33} so thou mistakest it, and therefore sputterest as if poisoned indeed. {Lam 3:19}
paragraphs.anchor: The cup of his fury.

paragraphs.text: Crassamentum, that thick stuff that settleth in the bottom, and usually is reserved for the worst of wicked ones, {Psa 75:8} while the saints sip only of the top of the cup. {a} See Eze 23:1-49; Eze 34:1-31.
paragraphs.anchor: Thou hast drunk the dregs.

paragraphs.text: Poeuhtm horrifieentissimum bibisti, exsuxisti, The cup of concussion or horror, as a just punishment of thy cup of slumbering and security, wherein thou hadst before caroused. {Isa 29:9-10}
paragraphs.anchor: Of the cup of trembling.

This was a point next the worst, as we say. She was without prudent and pious magistrates and ministers, or other friends to advise her; and so she was δισκακοδαιμων - twice miserable. Christ hath promised all his, "I will not leave you destitute," or orphans.
paragraphs.anchor: There is none to guide her.

paragraphs.text: Who should see to their aged parents and sublevate them, as pious Aeneas did, and as Scipio, who therehence had his name; but Zion’s sons were themselves in a dreadful plight, {Isa 51:20} and in an ill case to relieve their mother.
paragraphs.anchor: Among all her sons.

paragraphs.text: As they seldom are separated; as some write of the asp, that he never wanders alone without his companion.
paragraphs.anchor: These two things are come unto thee.

paragraphs.text: By whom but by myself, when thou art at thy greatest under, and even forsaken of thy hopes. See Isa 51:12.

paragraphs.text: Who shall drink it not to drunkenness only, as thou hast done, but unto madness. {Jer 25:10} Belshazzar and his Babylonians did so; the revenging hand of God was afterwards upon Antiochus, Vespasian, and his children; Antichristians drink of the wine of God’s wrath. {Rev 14:10}
